objective: Test whether line graphs increase perceived compound-growth acceleration and examine the complete proposed statistical pathway.

sample.population: CloudResearch participants who reported that they had not begun investing for retirement

exclusions.reason: Growth estimates indicated apparent misunderstanding of the response scale; at least one estimate exceeded twice the correct Year 40 estimate (55.6).
Undefined Estimated Growth Ratio because Year 20 and Year 30 estimates were equal.

projection.horizon: personalized from current age to age 65

estimated_growth_task.formula: (Year 40 growth estimate - Year 30 growth estimate) / (Year 30 growth estimate - Year 20 growth estimate)

interpretation.1: equal perceived increases in the earlier and later intervals
interpretation.>1: larger perceived increase in the later interval; stronger perceived acceleration

ability_confidence.interpretation: marginal direct effect; the ability-confidence serial indirect pathway was not significant

processing_fluency.interpretation: marginal direct effect; not a consistent explanation across the program

serial_mediation.causal_language_warning: Presentation condition was randomized. Estimated Growth Ratio, growth confidence, retirement-goal achievability, and planned contributions were measured. The serial indirect model is statistically consistent with the proposed pathway but does not independently establish causal ordering among the measured constructs.
